title: Deep Learning for Noise Reduction in High-Resolution In-Situ TEM
content: In-situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) is an essential technique for studying nanoparticles, providing valuable insights into their dynamic changes under various conditions, including phase transformations and structural deformations [1-3]. However, in-situ TEM images can often contain significant noise that obscures critical structural information and analysis at the atomic-level, as illustrated in Figure 1. The high noise level arises from (i) the use of a low electron dose to minimize sample damage, (ii) a high frame rate and short exposure time, and (iii) environmental instabilities, such as drift and vibrations during in-situ experiment [4].
